object_description: elongated bar with two lightweight volumes on a concrete base
design_condition: The elongated volume follows the street and integrates part of the existing pool structure, but its considerable footprint and narrow spacing dominate the park landscape and limit the quality of the surrounding open space.

positive.statement: The simple volume respectfully responds to the free form of the outdoor pool.
A spacious forecourt ensures good connections and activates the place.
Decentralized parking near the various entrances appears sensible and practical.
The proposed activities under the viaduct could ease the intensive use of the facility.
The swimming pool, ice-rink stand, and outdoor pool are accessible through a shared entrance hall.
The organization is compact and functional.
The attempt to integrate the existing swimming pool into the new volume is praiseworthy.
The volume offers a simple elegance and an abstract architectural expression.

negative.statement: The integration of the existing pool does not relieve the narrow space between the building and garden pool.
The large footprint and sealing provide no benefit to the open space.
The elongated bar dominates the park pool landscape, while the existing subtle topography is lost.
The proposed tree additions do not correspond to the existing tree concept, and biodiversity measures are insufficiently documented.
Access to the upper bathroom area is unattractive, with a narrow staircase and long routes.
The organization lacks flexibility for alternative access through the main entrance hall.
The small pavilion between the building and outdoor rink is operationally difficult and lacks nearby benches and cloakrooms.
The open ice rink is insufficiently shielded and requires additional noise protection.
The large volume and facade lead to high resource use, maintenance, heating, and lifecycle costs.
The desired simplicity produces indeterminacy and a lack of conciseness in the spatial organization and expression.
The project is the most expensive shortlisted proposal in construction costs.
